authors_reviews.title: Versatile foldable dog stretcher for medium to large dogs: I will keep it in my car in case!
authors_reviews.text: Upon receipt, I opened this very small box and a folded vinyl stretcher base popped out along with all these pipes, and I thought, oh no, I have to put it together (I was in no DIY mood), but not to fear. It was quite intuitive with or without the instructions and required only a minute or two to assemble. My last photo shows it folded, and I merely need to find a velcro strap or similar to hold it in its most compact form for the car. One could also completely disassemble for the most compact form, but then it would take precious time in an emergency to reassemble. So, off the bat, a positive impression.As referenced in many reviews, I have a beloved Aussie-Border Collie who is just shy of 15 years of age and whose hips and knee arthritis are catching up to her- despite the most aggressive veterinary care, though we still do a couple of miles pre-dawn around the lake, and she likes to wander around the enclosed dog park as well. Yet, the thought has most certainly occurred to me that she could just "quit" on me halfway into the walk, and it is unlikely I could carry a 50-pound dog all the way back. So, while a foldable garden wagon was one option, they take up so much space that I could not have it in the car continuously. This seemed the best alternative as it could remain in the back of my car while still letting me load groceries and the like. Plus, it would appear that for a lot of small cars with hatchbacks, once the back seats are folded down and the passenger seat pushed forward, the stretcher could be loaded with the dog and lie flat. The only question for me was whether I should opt for one with wheels, which seemed a good idea initially. But, I would not leave my dog unattended in the park and would need help carrying the stretcher, regardless, and I do meet other dog-walking friends at some point in the park walk. So, I opted for a more compact stretcher (42 inches x 8 inches folded) that would allow for two people to readily carry my 50-pound dog or another considerably larger and heavier (the stretcher is rated up to 260 pounds). So, theoretically, it could be used in emergencies for a child or adult able to sit up. Having it in the car might prove beneficial in ways never intended. (I hike trails in the Rocky Mountains, so snakebites and similar emergencies are always on my mind).I find this a very useful, durable, yet compact stretcher that I would feel confident in using to transport my beloved older "pup." Yes. Absolutely. Recommend.
authors_reviews.author: COProgressive

authors_reviews.title: Sturdy, Well-Made Emergency Stretcher—Hopefully Never Needed, But Good to Have
authors_reviews.text: This is one of those items you hope you never have to use, but it’s absolutely worth having on hand if you have larger dogs or live in a more rural setting.I haven’t had to use it in an actual emergency yet, but based on handling and inspecting it, the build quality is very solid. The main body is made from a thick, heavy-duty plastic material that feels durable enough to support weight without flexing excessively.The stitching throughout is reinforced, especially around the stress points like the strap attachments and the pockets where the support poles slide in. Those pole sleeves feel particularly well done, which is important since that’s where a lot of the load will be carried.The design is straightforward: you insert the support poles, and two people can carry a dog without having to awkwardly lift them, which is exactly what you want in an injury situation. It’s rated to hold up to around 132 pounds, so it should easily handle any of my dogs (my largest is about 95 pounds).It also includes securing straps, which is a big plus. Once you get a dog onto the stretcher, you can stabilize them so they’re not shifting around while being moved.I can think of quite a few scenarios where this would be useful—injuries, mobility issues, or even just transporting a large dog that can’t walk. Again, hopefully it never gets used, but in an emergency, having something like this ready could make a huge difference.Overall, this looks like a well-constructed, thoughtfully designed piece of emergency gear. It’s simple, strong, and gives you a much safer way to move a heavy dog when it matters most. And it stores very compactly in a quite small box so you can easily have it on hand at home or in a vehicle.
authors_reviews.author: NaturalHealth&NewTechnology

authors_reviews.title: Solid sturdy stretcher that’s a game changer for pet care.
authors_reviews.text: My last dog was 100 lbs and when he got suddenly ill in the middle of the night, we had to move him in a borrowed wheelbarrow, because we didn’t have one of these! I don’t think I need to expand on that story but you get the point: enormously stressful on top of enormously stressful. Oh how I miss him! We adopted a new fur baby (she’s 60 lbs) and never again want to be in a position to not be able to easily and safely move her if something happens, which brings me to this stretcher…This is a heavy, sturdy stretcher that will definitely be large enough to move her gently and the straps mean there will be minimum jostling, which is important in emergencies.It has aluminum poles so lighter weight but with a weight capacity of 260lbs, and solid stitching, I’m confident it will do the job without fear of further harm. It comes in a bunch of pieces but was easy to assemble, done in minutes!I got my pup comfortable with it by luring her with cookies and having her lie on it, after doing this several times over days, we gently lifted her (you need 2 people) and she lounged on it like a queen on her throne. After doing this process, I’m confident she’s not afraid of it, which will make it much easier to use in an emergency.We hike and knowing this is in my car and accessible brings me enormous relief. Great product that you hope you won’t need, but feel grateful that you have it just in case.
authors_reviews.author: Robin Jax

authors_reviews.title: Emergency pet stretcher
authors_reviews.text: This pet stretcher is one of those items you hope you’ll never need—but if you do, you’ll be incredibly glad to have it. It’s clearly designed with real-life emergencies in mind, especially for pet owners who have a pet they can’t easily lift or move on their own in the event of an emergency.The build quality is impressive right out of the box. The aluminum alloy frame reinforced with steel bars gives it a sturdy, dependable feel, and the 260 lb weight capacity adds real peace of mind. It doesn’t feel flimsy or like it might buckle under pressure—this is equipment you can trust in a stressful situation.What really stands out is the focus on safety. The adjustable straps keep pets secure without feeling overly restrictive, and the quick-release design means you’re not fumbling when time matters. The non-slip handles are another thoughtful touch—they provide a solid grip even if things are chaotic or your hands are wet.Cleanup is refreshingly simple. The material wipes down quickly, which is exactly what you want after an emergency or outdoor use. It feels durable and practical, not delicate or high-maintenance.Another big plus is how easy it is to store. It folds down quickly and compactly, so it won’t take up much space in a car or closet. That makes it realistic to keep on hand instead of being one of those bulky items you avoid storing.Whether you’re a pet owner, caregiver, or just someone who likes to be prepared, this stretcher fills a very real need. It’s reliable, well-designed, and practical—exactly what you want in an emergency tool.
authors_reviews.author: Meg Darling

authors_reviews.title: Pet transport stretcher - aluminum alloy
authors_reviews.text: This portable dog stretcher is sturdy and lightweight. The blue resting surface is 40" long and 25" wide (22" if you measure between the handles, rather than to the outside edges). There are three straps with quick-release buckles; they are each 2" wide and feel sturdy.The stretcher is very easy to assemble. It arrives with 2 hinged sections of aluminum alloy tubing, with 4 padded handles to attach to both ends of each. The hinged sections operate readily by squeezing a tab to release. In terms of storage space, you could easily return the unassembled stretcher to the package, it is very easy to re-assemble. The package is 11" x 17" x 2.75". If you prefer to assemble the stretcher and fold the hinged portion, you will need a space about 28" long and 6-7" in diameter to carry it.The stretcher feels well-made and sturdy. It will require 2 people to safely carry your pet. Also, there are no cross-pieces. That is, the weight of your pet will tend to cause the resting surface to sag toward the center. People carrying the stretcher will need to make sure to keep the handles separated while carrying.This is a lightweight, portable aid to transporting an ill or injured animal. It doesn't take up a lot of space and is easy to assemble, as well as to clean and store. I'm glad to have this.
authors_reviews.author: Amazon Reviewer

authors_reviews.title: Well made, easy assembly, note the length of bed for your needs.
authors_reviews.text: I have a folding cot on hand that can be used as a stretcher but always had in mind to get something better for my dogs if need be. I have large dogs; greyhounds.This stretcher was super easy to put together, and once it's together you don't need to break it down to store it, you can just fold it up and it takes up about as much room as a small folding camp chair. The fold joint is strong, and the metal bars are strong. The stretcher material is strong and I see no issue whatsoever with this well made stretcher. Keep in mind putting a blanker under the animal and them strapping the animal in within the blanket may be a better idea for panicky pets.My only caveat is that you need to make sure the bed of the stretcher is long enough for your pet if they should sustain a head or neck injury. I have very long body dogs, and unfortunately if my dog were unconscious the head would dangle. So keep in mind the length of the stretcher fabric vs. the length of your pet in a side prone position, and make sure it works for you.
authors_reviews.author: Internet User

authors_reviews.title: Nice, high quality doggy stretcher. You never know when you'll need something like this.
authors_reviews.text: I have a very large pup who I can't lift alone. If something were to happen to him, I would need someone to help me load him in my car for a trip to the vet. This stretcher would allow us to do that safely. I plan to keep it rolled up next to my front door where I can easily grab it for doggy road trips. As a former EMT, I've seen devices like this used to save pups from all sorts of misadventures. I'm happy to now have one for my pups.The device was very easy to put together. It took me less than 5 minutes. The tarp material is very thick and the straps are nice and thick. The whole thing is pretty light and easy to carry. I'm not sure how much weight it can carry as the listing says 260lbs but the images show 132lbs. My pup is 120lbs so hopefully it can securely hold that much.This is a nice upgrade to the tarp-like dog mover I currently carry in my car. Hopefully I never have to use it, but I'm confident it will do the job if the worst happens. I'm glad I got it.
authors_reviews.author: seastorm
